bandReport.notes:
Band covers items 24-42, consecutive, each appearing exactly once. Item 24 is whole on p14 (its Passage-4 heading is the first thing printed on p14-c1) and item 42 is whole on p22 (stem on p22-c2 with all four options above the Passage-3 heading), so nothing spills past either edge of the band.

DIRECTIONS BLOCKS AND PASSAGE MAPPING. Two comprehension blocks touch this band.

Block 1 - its preamble and Passages 1-3 are on p12, which is the PREVIOUS band; I do not own them and have not transcribed them. What my pages carry is its tail: Passage-4 (p14-c1) governing item 24, Passage-5 (p14-c1) governing item 25, Passage-6 (p14-c1 into p14-c2) governing item 26, and Passage-7 (p14-c2 into p16-c1) governing item 27. Each of these four passages governs EXACTLY ONE item - the booklet prints 'Passage-N', its text, then the single item that refers to it - so all four contexts are used by a single item and will raise a lonely-context warning at merge. That is the LEGITIMATE case the warning names (a directions block giving each item its own passage), not per-item material parked in context. From the numbering the block is almost certainly 'the following 7 items' over 'seven passages' covering items 21-27, of which the previous band owns 21-23; a reader reconciling the paper should confirm that preamble off p12 rather than take my inference for it, since I never saw it.

Block 2 begins at the top of p22-c1 and reads: 'Directions for the following 8 (eight) items : Read the following seven passages and answer the items that follow the passages. Your answers to these items should be based on the passages only.' Verified at 2x. It covers items 41-48, of which only 41 and 42 fall in this band. Its Passage-1 (p22-c1) governs item 41 and its Passage-2 (p22-c1 into p22-c2) governs item 42, one item each. NOTE FOR THE NEXT BAND: 8 items over 7 passages means exactly ONE passage in this block governs TWO items, and that passage is in the next band's territory (items 43-48), not mine. Also for the next band - Passage-3 of this block STARTS at the foot of p22-c2, below item 42's options, and its item is on p24. I have deliberately not transcribed it because I own no item under it; its opening words are 'We live in digital times. The digital is not just something we use strategically and specifically to do a few tasks. Our very perception of who we are, how we connect to the world around us, and the ways in which we define our domains of' and it continues onto p24.

No 'Directions for the following N items' preamble and no 'Passage - N' label is inside any context; contexts hold passage prose only.

DECIMAL SEPARATOR - RAISED MIDDLE DOT. This booklet sets the decimal point as a raised MIDDLE DOT, and I have PRESERVED it as U+00B7. The only decimals in this band are item 28's options (b) '47\u00b75 kg' and (d) '52\u00b75 kg'; both were verified at 2x, where the dot clearly sits at mid-x-height rather than on the baseline. No item in this band prints a decimal with an ordinary full stop, so I found NO intra-paper inconsistency on my pages - but I can only speak for pages 14-22 and the other bands should be checked against this before the paper is called consistent.

COLUMN CROPS. All ten column crops on my five pages are clean. None is sliced, no item number is missing from the top of a c2, and no option block is cut. Every c2 crop carries a thin sliver of the neighbouring column's line-end letters down its far-left margin (e.g. 'n / in / t. / n / d' down the left edge of p14-c2) - that is the expected overlap, not a slice. All text was read from the c1/c2 crops in the order c1 top-to-bottom then c2 top-to-bottom; the whole-page images were not needed for reading order on any page. Passage-6 (p14-c1 to p14-c2), Passage-7 (p14-c2 to p16-c1) and Passage-2 of block 2 (p22-c1 to p22-c2) each flow across a column or page break and were stitched from the two column crops.

SCAN DEGRADATION - WORDS RESTORED, NOT 'CORRECTED'. This scan is a photocopy generation in which the enclosed counter of 'e' is sometimes filled with ink, so an 'e' reads as a 'c'. Four places were magnified to 2x and read in context before transcription, and in each the printed word is unambiguous: Passage-4 'anarchy; it is to refuse one's political' (renders as 'aualcliy ... rcfusc onc's'); Passage-7 'the lessons they contain for those of us' (the 'f' of 'for' has a degraded crossbar); item 40 option (b) 'Neha' (renders as 'Ncha', and the stem three lines above prints 'Neha obtained more marks than Randhir'); item 30 option (c) 'P is equal to Q' (renders as 'P ia equal to Q'). These are scanner artefacts on words the booklet spells correctly, NOT printed typos, so they are transcribed as the words. I found no genuine compositor typo in this band.

VERBATIM ODDITIES PRESERVED. Passage-2 of block 2 prints 'since 1990s.' with no apostrophe and no article - verified at 2x and transcribed exactly as printed. Item 32 uses the Indian Rupee sign; verified at 2x (the lower stroke is ink-degraded but the double-barred R is unmistakable) and transcribed as U+20B9. The booklet's space-before-colon style is preserved ('have been made :', 'Statement :', 'Conclusions :', 'that follow :'), as is the em dash in Passage-7 ('enabled the winners to win-and certain', U+2014) and in Passage-2 of block 2 ('three factors-political legitimacy', U+2014).

EMPHASIS. Items 41 and 42 print an emphasised phrase in bold italic - 'best' in item 41, and 'most logical, rational and critical inference' in item 42. These are rendered as markdown '**...**', following the existing convention in this corpus (a shipped Paper II band uses '**not**' the same way). The emphasis is part of what the item asks, so dropping it would change the question; a reader who prefers the plain form should strip the asterisks in both items together.

TYPOGRAPHY NORMALISED. Curly quotation marks and apostrophes are transcribed as straight ASCII ' and " throughout, following the dominant convention of the shipped Paper II corpus. This affects the quoted assertion in Passage-7 and the possessives/contractions in Passage-4, item 33 ('o'clock') and elsewhere. The raised middle dot above is the one glyph deliberately NOT normalised, because it is semantically a decimal point.

COLLISION CHECK. Four items in this band share the identical four-option set (1 only / 2 only / Both 1 and 2 / Neither 1 nor 2): 26, 27 and 34. Items 26 and 27 additionally share the identical opening sentence 'With reference to the above passage, the following assumptions have been made :' - they are distinguished ONLY by their numbered statement lists, which are therefore kept in the STEM and not in the context, so their stems and their content hashes stay distinct. Item 34 differs in stem outright. I checked all 19 stem+option pairs in this band against one another and found no collision. No item has duplicate option text.

SUBTOPIC WARNING. Item 33 (a clock that strikes n times at n o'clock; time taken is proportional to the INTERVALS between strikes, not the strikes) has no good match in the catalog's Clocks and Calendars subtopics - 'Clocks and Angles' and 'Faulty Clocks and Gaining Time' both misdescribe it - so it carries the ad-hoc subtopic 'Clock Strikes and Intervals'.

SCRATCH-FILE COLLISION OBSERVED (process note, no effect on this data). An early magnification crop written to the generic path '/tmp/z1.png' came back showing content from a DIFFERENT part of the paper - almost certainly a concurrently-running band agent writing the same filename, since Python on this box resolves '/tmp' to 'C:\tmp', a shared working directory. Every crop after that was written to a band-namespaced scratch directory and re-verified. No transcription in this file rests on the collided read.

No defective questions, no duplicate options, no skipped numbers, and no page in this band was empty.

questions.context: The greatest blessing that technological progress has in store for mankind is not, of course, an accumulation of material possessions. The amount of these that can be effectively enjoyed by one individual in one lifetime is not great. But there is not the same narrow limit to the possibilities of the enjoyment of leisure. The gift of leisure may be abused by people who have had no experience of making use of it. Yet the creative use of leisure by a minority in societies has been the mainspring of all human progress beyond the primitive level.
questions.stem:
With reference to the above passage, the following assumptions have been made :
1. People always see the leisure time as a gift and use it for acquiring more material possessions.
2. Use of leisure by some people to produce new and original things has been the chief source of human progress.
Which of these assumptions is/are valid?

And the student will see that the same pattern recurs consistently, again and again, throughout the centuries.

questions.context: Disruption of traditional institutions, identifications and loyalties is likely to lead to ambivalent situations. It is possible that some people may renew their identification with traditional groups whereas others align themselves with new groups and symbols emergent from processes of political development. In addition, political development tends to foster group awareness of a variety of class, tribe, region, clan, language, religion, occupation and others.

options.label: B

options.label: C

questions.context: There has been a significant trend worldwide towards regionalism in government, resulting in a widespread transfer of powers downwards towards regions and communities since 1990s. This process, which involves the creation of new political entities and bodies at a sub-national level and an increase in their content and powers, is known as devolution. Devolution has been characterized as being made up of three factors—political legitimacy, decentralization of authority and decentralization of resources. Political legitimacy here means a mass demand from below for the decentralization process, which is able to create a political force for it to take place. In many cases, decentralization is initiated by the upper tier of government without sufficient political mobilization for it at the grassroots level, and in such cases the decentralization process often does not fulfil its objectives.
questions.stem: Which among the following is the **most logical, rational and critical inference** that can be made from the above passage?

options.label: A
options.text: Emergence of powerful mass leaders is essential to create sub-national political entities and thus ensure successful devolution and decentralization.

options.label: B
options.text: The upper tier of government should impose devolution and decentralization on the regional communities by law or otherwise.

options.label: C
options.text: Devolution, to be successful, requires a democracy in which there is free expression of the will of the people at lower level and their active participation at the grassroots level.

options.label: D
options.text: For devolution to take place, a strong feeling of regionalism in the masses is essential.
